fichas.title: Composite concrete wall constructions
fichas.summary: Reinforced concrete walls may be cast on site or precast. Solid concrete used externally requires additional thermal insulation, either as an external insulation system or as a multi-leaf construction. Two-layer reinforced concrete walls with core insulation are used particularly for large-format external wall elements.

fichas.title: Timber-framed and insulated masonry walls
fichas.summary: The page illustrates timber-framed walls, log-house construction, and masonry walls with external insulation or cladding. Timber framing is described as economical and common, with vertical loads transferred through studs; framed panels may be prefabricated with thermal insulation. Timber walls require sufficient roof overhang and replaceable cladding in splash areas.

fichas.title: Non-load-bearing external walls and curtain walls
fichas.summary: Light, often prefabricated panels are used as non-load-bearing external walls in framed buildings, reducing load at slab edges and enabling rapid assembly and later replacement. Curtain walls may use prefabricated metal-glass construction, façade panels, multi-layer façade elements with windows and parapets, or precast concrete elements. They are commonly fixed to slabs or framed columns with brackets or anchors.
